sections.overview: Plectrophenax nivalis is a small passerine that breeds across the Arctic and winters farther south. Its closest species-level relative is McKay’s Bunting (Plectrophenax hyperboreus), and phylogenetic work treats the pair as sister species.
sections.identification: The plumage is strongly patterned in black and white during the breeding season and becomes browner in winter; the sexes also differ in appearance.
sections.habitat: It nests in rocky tundra and crevices across circumpolar Arctic regions, then uses open fields, coasts and other barren ground in winter.
sections.diet: It takes seeds and other plant material for much of the year, adding small invertebrates during the breeding season.
sections.behavior: Outside the breeding season it often forages and roosts in flocks, sometimes gathering in large groups.
sections.reproduction: It places a grass-and-moss nest deep in a rock crevice, where the female incubates while the male brings food.
sections.ecology: Its seasonal movements link Arctic breeding habitat with temperate wintering areas; in winter it feeds mainly on seeds on the ground.
sections.conservation: The latest IUCN assessment available in the consulted account lists it as Least Concern, with a decreasing global trend noted.
